title: ReviewMap: Mapping Evaluative Acts and Automation Boundaries in Peer-Review Comments
abstract: arXiv:2611.07489v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Peer-review comments check what a paper does and judge why it matters, but no existing scheme distinguishes these two evaluative acts. We argue that making these acts explicit and measuring how reliably LLMs identify them is a prerequisite for responsible LLM-assisted review analysis: humans need to inspect review judgments and their grounds. This defines a more honest mission for NLP in peer review than full automation. We present ReviewMap, a framework that classifies each comment as assessment of claims and scholarly standards or calibration of contribution value and venue fit, with finer-grained attributes applied conditionally by act type. translated_title: ReviewMap：绘制同行评审评论中的评估行为与自动化边界
translated_abstract: 同行评审评论既要核查论文做了什么，又要评判其为何重要，但目前尚无现有方案能够区分这两种评估行为。我们认为，使这些行为显性化并衡量大语言模型（LLM）识别它们的可靠程度，是负责任地开展 LLM 辅助评审分析的前提：人类需要能够审查评审判断及其依据。这为 NLP 在同行评审中确立了一个比全面自动化更诚实的使命。我们提出了 ReviewMap，该框架将每条评论分类为对论文主张与学术标准的评估，或对贡献价值与会议契合度的校准，并根据行为类型有条件地应用更细粒度的属性。通过多模型 LLM 共识将该框架应用于 500 篇 ICLR 2026 论文，结果表明行为层在操作准则下（模型间 κ ≥ 0.75）可被可靠地自动化，并得到对 470 条开发评论的五人人工验证支持，而属性层则需要人工监督……
tldr: 该论文提出 ReviewMap 框架，将同行评审评论区分为“主张与学术标准评估”和“贡献价值与会议契合度校准”两类行为，证明行为层可通过多模型 LLM 共识可靠地自动化（κ≥0.75），而属性层仍需人工监督，从而为 NLP 在同行评审中确立了比全面自动化更务实、更诚实的定位。
en_tdlr: ReviewMap classifies peer-review comments into assessment and calibration acts, demonstrating that the act layer can be reliably automated via multi-model LLM consensus (κ≥0.75) while the attribute layer requires human oversight—defining a more honest mission for NLP in peer review than full automation.
